messages.author: 528560773e2cb27f
messages.subject: Covariance matrices in an array
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to analyze vector time series data in RStan. Assuming that a vector time series was taken at multiple sites, I intended to specify different covariance matrix for each site. This was done by embedding covariance matrices in an array with a dimension I (i.e., number of the sites) like:

parameters {
    ...
    cov_matrix[N] Sigma[I];
    ...
}
model {
    ...
    for (i in 1:I) {
        for (t in 2:T) {
            y[t, i] ~ multi_normal(mu_y_t, Sigma[i]);
    ...
}

where both y[t, i] and mu_y_t were specified as vectors of length N. When I run this model, however, I got the following error messages:

LOCATION:  file=input; line=19, column=17

                y[t, i] ~ multi_normal(mu_y_t, Sigma[i]);
                ^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
    arg 0 type=vector
    arg 1 type=vector
    arg 2 type=row vector
unknown distribution=multi_normal
Parser expecting: "}"


which seems that here Sigma might be recognized in Stan as a matrix, rather than an array.

Was this a wrong approach to model multiple covariance matrices in Stan? Follwing is an R code which would reconstruct this error.

library(rstan)
 
model_code <- '
    data {
        int<lower = 0> T;
        int<lower = 0> I;
        int<lower = 0> N;
        vector[N] y[T, I];
        int<lower = 0> df;
        cov_matrix[N] sm;
    }
    parameters {
        cov_matrix[N] Sigma[I];
    }
    model {
        for (t in 2:T) {
            for (i in 1:I) {
                vector[N] mu_y_t;
                for (n in 1:N)
                    mu_y_t[n] <- y[n, t-1, i];
                y[t, i] ~ multi_normal(mu_y_t, Sigma[i]);
            }
        }
        for (i in 1:I)
            Sigma[i] ~ wishart(df, sm);
    }
'

T <- 20; I <- 10; N <- 3
y <- array(rnorm(T * I * N), dim = c(T, I, N))

data <- list(T = T, I = I, N = N, y = y,
             df = N, sm = diag(N))

fit <- stan(model_code = model_code, data = data)


Regards,

Keiichi

----
Keiichi FUKAYA, Ph.D.
Faculty of Environmental Science
Hokkaido University

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Covariance matrices in an array
parts:
Thanks for the clear bug report.

This is a bug in type inference that I'll fix
right away.

Here's the simplest model that tickles the bug:

data {
vector[5] y[10];
vector[5] mu[10];
}
parameters {
cov_matrix[5] Sigma[10];
}
model {
for (n in 1:10)
y[n] ~ multi_normal(mu[n],Sigma[n]);
}

which produces the following error:

ERROR PARSING
LOCATION: file=input; line=10, column=7

y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i],Sigma[i]);

^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
arg 0 type=vector
arg 1 type=vector
arg 2 type=row vector
unknown distribution=multi_normal

Parser expecting: <statement>

We should be releasing 1.0.2 (or 1.1.0) later
this week or next week, and the fix will go in it.
I'll post back to this list when it's fixed, so
if you're using the command line version and
want to grab the latest version from version control,
that would work until we release 1.0.2.

Until then, there's not a good workaround due
to the problem with type inference.

- Bob
